task.title: Persist durable one-shot schedule intent
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/789 with an inert event-sourced schedule boundary and deterministic caller-cutoff due discovery.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip exact schedule identity, task goal, and Unix-millisecond due instant through reopen while rejecting duplicate identities.
Return pending schedules due at or before a caller-owned cutoff in due-instant then exact-ID order.
Exclude future and unrelated streams and fail closed on malformed owning streams or invalid history.
Keep clock reads, task creation, dispatch, recurrence, retries, and permission outside this boundary.

attempts.diagnostic: The focused integration target failed because the scheduler module and public contract did not exist.
attempts.patch: Added reopen, duplicate, inclusive-cutoff, deterministic-ordering, unrelated-stream, malformed-payload, and invalid-history tests first.

attempts.summary: Implemented immutable one-shot intent over the typed event log.
attempts.diagnostic: Ambient clock access or automatic task creation would have combined time and execution authority before either policy existed.
attempts.patch: Added validated opaque identities, exact caller-owned instants, one version-one creation event, fail-closed replay, and snapshot-consistent due discovery.

attempts.summary: Refactored around the existing persistence substrate and verified the boundary.
attempts.diagnostic: Independent and substantive hosted review found no blocking correctness issue at the merged head.
attempts.patch: Kept one immutable event and reused event-log replay and authoritative event discovery; documented ADR-0034 and focused scheduler behavior.

outcome.summary: The kernel now persists inert one-shot task intent and deterministically discovers due schedules without owning a clock or execution decision.

verification.command: nix develop --command cargo test --locked -p vela-kernel --test schedule_store

lessons: Persist intent before combining it with clock, dispatch, retry, or permission policy.
Caller-owned cutoff input keeps due selection deterministic and directly testable.
Authoritative creation-event discovery avoids a second mutable schedule index.
Fail closed on malformed candidate streams instead of returning a trustworthy-looking partial due set.
